subject: The new and huger Paramount has a new co-CEO
posts:
Paramount names Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz as co-CEO ahead of its massive Warner Bros. Discovery merger.
Evidence: Corporate consolidation, Mattel leadership, elite executive shuffle
#Aletheia #Media #Paramount

Paramount claims Ynon Kreiz will join David Ellison to jointly lead the combined media giant, focusing on day-to-day management and integration.
Stated Judgement: (+1.0, 0.0) — Good Preference

Behind the corporate PR gloss lies a massive $110B consolidation driven by elite capital (Larry Ellison's Oracle fortune) and legal settlements, locking down media control.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.8, -0.9) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Massive media consolidation is framed as creative synergy, masking elite financial extraction and corporate centralization.

Integrity: Severe Deception (Hypocrisy: 12.5, z: 2)

- Corporate Mergers: FAIL (-0.85, -0.90) — Masks wealth concentration as innovation.
- Executive Shuffling: PASS (0.00, 0.00) — Standard corporate management transition.
David Ellison is placing outgoing Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz as co-CEO of the newly combined Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery empire, expected to close in October.

The Bright Side:
Experienced executives like Kreiz bring operational stability to traditional studio assets facing massive digital disruption.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Confusing WHAT (executive appointment) with WHO (elite capital interests controlling the media landscape).

Social Physics Analysis:
David Ellison and elite backers run a Smart Selfish Maneuver, using corporate restructuring and legal settlements as pretexts to centralize immense media power while projecting stability.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Deception. High corporate centralization yields extractive media monopolies.

The Unavoidable Truth: Massive media mergers concentrate cultural power in the hands of elite financial dynasties.

The Unavoidable Lie: Corporate executive appointments represent neutral creative synergies.

Alethekanon:
Corporate restructuring is routinely sanitized as creative vision, concealing the relentless centralization of cultural power.

Awwthekanon:
It is disheartening to watch monolithic media empires swallow up cultural spaces, treating storytellers and viewers merely as assets on a balance sheet.

Brothekanon:
Just another billionaire media shuffle where the rich guys trade chairmanships while everyone else worries about streaming price hikes.

Spirithekanon:
"Do not wear yourself out to get rich; do not rely on your own cleverness." Proverbs 23:4 FAIL
Chasing infinite corporate scale blinds leaders to the human cost of endless consolidation.

Paramount is appointing a new co-CEO ahead of the close of its $110 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. Ynon Kreiz, previously Mattel’s chairman and CEO, will be joining Paramount to lead alongside chairman and CEO David Ellison.

According to Paramount, “Ellison will focus on the company’s long-term strategy, creative vision and direction, including its talent relationships, strategic partnerships, technology and capital allocation. Kreiz will focus on the company’s day-to-day management and integration of the combined businesses.” The combined Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery will “report jointly” to Ellison and Kreiz.

Kreiz joined Mattel in 2018. While he was leading the company, it launched the hit Barbie film in partnership with Warner Bros. Pictures. His first day at Paramount is October 5th.

Today, a judge also approved Paramount’s recently-announced settlement in a lawsuit with several states that had been blocking the Warner Bros. Discovery merger, according to Reuters.

On Tuesday, Paramount’s streaming chief, Cindy Holland, announced that she would be stepping down, and Variety reports that HBO boss Casey Bloys is “poised” to take over both Paramount Plus and HBO.
